github.abstract: CLI-Anything: Making ALL Software Agent-Native Today's Software Serves Humans👨‍💻. Tomorrow's Users will be Agents🤖. CLI-Anything: Bridging the Gap Between AI Agents and the World's Software 🌐 CLI-Hub : pip install cli-anything-hub then cli-hub install <name> — browse, install, and manage all community-built CLIs. Want to add your own? Open a PR — the hub updates instantly. 🎬 See Demos : Watch AI agents use generated CLIs plus preview, live preview, and trajectory loops to produce real artifacts — CAD builds, 3D scenes, diagrams, gameplay, subtitles, and more. 🙋 [Become a Contributor, or Request a CLI] : Join us ! Sign up to build a new CLI harness — once reviewed and merged, you'll gain access as one of our community contributors! Wish CLI-Anything supported a specific software or service? Submit a wishlist request ! One Command Line : Make any software agent-ready for Pi, OpenClaw, nanobot, Cursor, Claude Code, etc. 中文文件 | 日本語ドキュメント | Deutsch 📰 News Thanks to all invaluable efforts from the community! More updates continuously on the way everyday.. 2026-05-30 🧭 Hermes skill proposed (#320), adding a CLI-Anything orchestration skill with installer scripts and HARNESS fallback guidance. 🗺️ ArcGIS Pro was proposed for the public registry (#318) as a Windows/ArcPy CLI for cartography, geoprocessing, feature editing, and live-Pro MCP workflows. 2026-05-27 🔧 CLI-Hub registry date updates now handle python -m pip install commands (#312), improving package-date detection for registry automation. 2026-05-23 📝 Obsidian Agent CLI was proposed for the public registry (#307), bringing a PyPI-installed Obsidian automation CLI with persistent agent memory workflows and a pinned skill link. 2026-05-21 🔒 Sketch CLI token-file handling was hardened against path traversal and symlink escapes (#304). 2026-05-20 📓 Joplin CLI was proposed (#300) with notebooks, notes, to-dos, tags, attachments, search/sync, import/export, server/E2EE helpers, full docs, packaged skill docs, and a 134-test validation baseline. 2026-05-20 🎛️ Rekordbox CLI merged (#252) with guarded SQLCipher write paths, backup-required forced writes, smoke coverage, and root skill sync. 📚 Calibre CLI merged (#223) with library/search/metadata/conversion/export workflows, 41 unit tests, real-Calibre E2E evidence, and root skill validation. 🧊 3MF CLI merged (#209) with mesh inspection, hole resizing, repair, comparison, and preserved triangle attributes. 🎙️ MiniMax CLI merged (#189) with chat/TTS workflows, JSON-safe model/voice listing, REPL quote handling, and smoke/E2E coverage. 🎮 UEAtelier joined the registry (#297) as an Unreal Editor MCP self-extension workbench with a Python CLI proxy. 2026-05-19 🛠️ Existing harnesses got a quality/security pass — Zoom downloads recordings from direct URLs (#294), Obsidian search now uses the Local REST API vendor content types (#289), LibreOffice headless conversion is more robust on macOS (#290), and XML/SVG/ODF/MLT/MusicXML/CSL parsing now routes untrusted input through defusedxml (#296). 2026-05-18 📈 README presentation refreshed with the Trendshift badge and centered project header polish (#285, #286), keeping the landing section focused on discovery and project momentum. 2026-05-17 🌐 CLI-Hub registry handling was hardened (#281) — registry entries are now copied before _source tagging, preventing cached or mocked registry data from being mutated in place. 2026-05-16 🔧 n8n received the REPL banner crash fix that later merged into main (#280), restoring the no-subcommand interactive startup path with regression coverage. Earlier news (Apr 10–18) 2026-04-18 🧩 All SKILL.md files are now being unified under the top-level skills/ directory — every CLI skill can be installed from one canonical source with npx skills add HKUDS/CLI-Anything --skill <skill-name> -g -y . We also added root-skill validation CI, synced contribution / PR docs and REPL skill-path hints to the new layout, and refreshed the CLI-Hub install-first frontend around the new npx skills flow. 2026-04-17 🌐 CLI-Hub received another install UX pass — public registry metadata and skill coverage were tightened, visit counting was corrected, and the web hub was further refined. 🧪 Shotcut render output duration was fixed (#92). 📝 SKILL contribution paths were corrected for the new docs flow (#224), and the skill generator now safely handles empty intros (#203). 2026-04-16 🗺️ QGIS CLI merged (#207) — a full GIS / map authoring harness landed. 🧬 UniMol Tools CLI merged (#219) for molecular modeling workflows. 🌐 CLI-Hub also added more public CLIs, including py4csr , refreshed its generated meta-skill, corrected SKILL contribution docs, and fixed apt-get package extraction in skill generation (#204). 2026-04-16 📈 Unreal Insights CLI expanded — added background capture session control ( capture start/status/snapshot/stop ), engine-root-matched UnrealInsights.exe resolution/build flows, and refreshed docs/tests for the new orchestration workflow. 2026-04-15 🌐 CLI-Hub updated to v0.2.0 — the PyPI package now supports public CLIs from multiple install sources ( pip , npm , brew , bundled/system tools), backed by a new public_registry.json . The Hub frontend was redesigned with separate CLI-Anything CLIs and Public CLIs decks, and live end-to-end checks now cover real install, update, and uninstall flows across both pip and npm packages. 2026-04-14 🧭 Safari CLI merged (#212) and added to the Hub registry — browser automation via safari-mcp . 🎬 Kdenlive also received compatibility fixes for Gen 5 project output and invalid project generation. 2026-04-13 📓 Obsidian CLI merged (#211) — knowledge management harness via the Local REST API, with 48 unit tests and 7 E2E tests. ⛓️ Eth2-Quickstart CLI merged (#195) — Ethereum staking node management harness. 📚 Zotero CLI updated to v0.4.1 (#201) — now shipped from its standalone repo, and CLI-Hub gained support for remote skill_md URLs. 2026-04-11 🔗 n8n CLI merged (#188) — workflow automation harness for self-hosted automation flows. 🔧 Exa CLI fix (#205) added the x-exa-integration header for usage tracking. 📦 CLI-Hub also gained its PyPI auto-publish workflow and package refresh pipeline. 2026-04-10 📦 CLI-Hub package manager launched — pip install cli-anything-hub to browse, search, install, update, and uninstall CLI-Anything harnesses from one command. The web Hub also shipped its first install-focused frontend refresh and "Empower yourself" toolkit card. Earlier news (Apr 1–9) 2026-04-09 🧹 Cleanup and docs pass (#200) — fixed Openscreen test subtotals, added Openscreen to the Chinese README and project structure, and clarified /cli-anything command syntax in the docs. 2026-04-08 🎬 Openscreen CLI merged (#183) — screen recording editor harness with 101 tests. ☁️ CloudAnalyzer CLI merged (#181) — cloud cost analysis harness with 27 commands. 🌊 SeaClip / PM2 / ChromaDB harnesses merged (#129). 2026-04-07 🔄 Dify Workflow CLI merged (#191) — workflow automation wrapper. 🔧 Inkscape auto-save fix (#193, fixes #182). 🛡️ DomShell security hardening (#156) — URL validation and DOM sanitization for the browser CLI. 🥧 Pi Coding Agent extension merged (#178). 2026-04-06 🔍 Exa CLI merged (#172) — AI-powered web search and answers harness. 🎮 Godot CLI merged (#140) — game engine harness with a full demo-game E2E pipeline. ☁️ CloudAnalyzer review fixes and frontend improvements also landed. 2026-04-03 🧪 WireMock CLI merged (#170) — HTTP mock server harness for API testing. 🥧 Pi Coding Agent extension support also landed, and CLI demo recordings were added to the docs. 2026-04-01 ⚔️ Slay the Spire II CLI merged (#148) — deck-building roguelike harness. 🎥 VideoCaptioner CLI merged (#166) — AI-powered video captioning harness. 🛰️ IntelWatch was added to the registry for B2B OSINT workflows. Earlier news (Mar 23–30) 2026-03-30 🏗️ CLI-Anything v0.2.0 — HARNESS.md progressive disclosure redesign. Detailed guides extracted into guides/ for on-demand loading. Phases 1–7 now contiguous.

github.title: jingyaogong/minimind
github.abstract:
"大道至簡" 中文 | English 此開源專案旨在完全從 0 開始，僅用 3 塊錢成本與 2 小時訓練時間，即可訓練出規模約為 64M 的超小語言模型 MiniMind。 MiniMind 系列極其輕量，主線最小版本體積約為 GPT-3 的 $\frac{1}{2700}$ ，力求讓普通個人 GPU 也能快速完成訓練與復現。 專案同時開源了大模型的極簡結構與完整訓練鏈路，覆蓋 MoE、資料清洗、預訓練（Pretrain）、監督微調（SFT）、LoRA、RLHF（DPO）、RLAIF（PPO / GRPO / CISPO）、Tool Use、Agentic RL、自適應思考與模型蒸餾等全過程程式碼。 MiniMind 同時拓展了視覺模態模型 MiniMind-V 、多模態 Omni 模型 MiniMind-O 、擴散語言模型（MiniMind-dLM）、線性模型（MiniMind-Linear），詳見 Discussion 。 專案所有核心演算法程式碼均從 0 使用 PyTorch 原生實現，不依賴第三方庫提供的高層抽象介面。 這不僅是一個大語言模型全階段開源復現專案，也是一套面向 LLM 入門與實踐的教程。 希望此專案能為更多人提供一個可復現、可理解、可擴展的起點，一起感受創造的樂趣，並推動更廣泛 AI 社群的進步。 注：本專案基於 Apache 2.0 協議開源，完全免費。“2 小時” 指 SFT 階段在單張 NVIDIA 3090 上跑完 1 epoch 的實測耗時，“3 塊錢” 指對應時段的 GPU 租用成本。 🔗 線上體驗 | 🔗 影片介紹 ❤️ 贊助 MiniMind × Infistar.cc ：Claude、GPT、Gemini、DeepSeek等200+模型一個Key搞定，低至官方0.1折（省99%），100%官方純血可驗真，千條線路自動切換。通過 專屬連結 註冊即送¥5。 關於贊助與合作 MiniMind 以 Apache 2.0 協議完全開源、永久免費。贊助完全自願，不換取任何特權，也不影響專案使用。感謝每一位支持者，讓這個業餘時間維護的專案得以持續。 贊助方式包括按月佔位，或直接贊助 GPU 伺服器（算力可能用於專案相關或不相關的研究性探索）。 如有意向，歡迎通過 郵件 聯絡。 📌 專案介紹 大語言模型（Large Language Model, LLM）的出現，引發了全球範圍內對 AI 的空前關注。無論是 ChatGPT、DeepSeek 還是 Qwen，都以驚豔的效果讓人真切感受到這場技術浪潮的衝擊力。然而，動輒數百億參數的模型規模，使得它們對個人裝置而言不僅難以訓練，甚至連部署都顯得遙不可及。開啟大模型的“黑盒子”，真正去理解其內部運作機制，本應是一件令人心潮澎湃的事。遺憾的是，絕大多數探索最終都止步於使用 LoRA 等技術對現有大模型做少量微調，學習一些新指令或特定任務。這更像是在教牛頓如何使用 21 世紀的智慧手機——雖然有趣，卻偏離了理解物理本質的初衷。 與此同時，第三方的大模型框架與工具庫，如 transformers / trl / peft 等，往往只暴露出高度抽象的介面。只需短短十幾行程式碼，就可以完成“載入模型 + 載入資料集 + 推理 + 強化學習”的全流程訓練。這種高效封裝固然便利，卻也在一定程度上把開發者與底層實現隔離開來，削弱了深入理解 LLM 核心程式碼的機會。我認為 “用樂高自己拼出一架飛機，遠比坐在頭等艙裡飛行更讓人興奮”，然而更現實的問題是，網際網路上充斥著大量付費課程和營銷內容，用漏洞百出、一知半解的講解包裝所謂的 AI 教程。正因如此，本專案的初衷就是儘可能降低 LLM 的學習門檻，讓每個人都能從理解每一行程式碼開始，從 0 開始親手訓練一個極小的語言模型。是的，從 零開始訓練 ，而不是僅僅停留在 推理 層面。最低只需不到 3 塊錢的伺服器成本，就能親身體驗從 0 到 1 構建一個語言模型的全過程。 😊 一起感受創造的樂趣吧！ 🎉 本專案包含以下內容 提供完整的 MiniMind-LLM 結構程式碼（Dense + MoE），當前主線結構對齊 Qwen3 / Qwen3-MoE 生態。 提供 Tokenizer 與分詞器訓練程式碼，支援 <tool_call> 、 <tool_response> 、 <think> 等模板標記。 覆蓋 Pretrain、SFT、LoRA、RLHF-DPO、RLAIF（PPO / GRPO / CISPO）、Tool Use、Agentic RL、自適應思考與模型蒸餾等完整訓練流程。 提供全階段開源資料，覆蓋收集、蒸餾、清洗與去重後的高質量資料集。 關鍵訓練演算法與核心模組均從 0 實現，不依賴第三方框架封裝。 相容 transformers 、 trl 、 peft 等主流框架，以及 llama.cpp 、 vllm 、 ollama 等常用推理引擎與 Llama-Factory 等訓練框架。 支援單機單卡與單機多卡（DDP、DeepSpeed）訓練，支援 wandb / swanlab 視覺化與動態啟停訓練。 支援在 C-Eval、C-MMLU、OpenBookQA 等第三方測評集上進行評測，並支援通過 YaRN 實現 RoPE 長文本外推。 提供相容 OpenAI API 協議的極簡服務端，便於接入 FastGPT、Open-WebUI 等第三方 Chat UI，並支援 reasoning_content 、 tool_calls 、 open_thinking 。 提供基於 Streamlit 的極簡聊天 WebUI，支援思考展示、工具選擇與多輪 Tool Call。 包含實驗性拓展：離散擴散語言模型（ dLM ）與線性注意力模型（ Linear Attention ），均可基於主線 AR 模型進行續訓。 🎉 已釋出模型列表 模型 參數量 Release minimind-3 64M 2026.04.01 minimind-3-moe 198M-A64M 2026.04.01 minimind2-small 26M 2025.04.26 minimind2-moe 145M 2025.04.26 minimind2 104M 2025.04.26 minimind-v1-small 26M 2024.08.28 minimind-v1-moe 4×26M 2024.09.17 minimind-v1 108M 2024.09.01 📝 更新日誌 🔥 2026-04-01 釋出 minimind-3 / minimind-3-moe ：結構、Tokenizer、訓練鏈路、推理介面與預設配置全面更新 結構主線對齊 Qwen3 / Qwen3-MoE 生態：Dense 約 64M ，MoE 約 198M-A64M ，並移除了 shared expert 設計 預設訓練資料切換為 pretrain_t2t(_mini).jsonl 、 sft_t2t(_mini).jsonl 、 rlaif.jsonl 、 agent_rl.jsonl 與 agent_rl_math.jsonl 移除獨立 train_reason.py ；思考能力統一由 chat_template + <think> 與 open_thinking 自適應開關控制 toolcall 能力已混入 sft_t2t / sft_t2t_mini 主線資料，預設 full_sft 即具備基礎 Tool Call 能力；同時新增 scripts/chat_api.py 等推理示例 新增原生 Agentic RL 訓練指令碼 train_agent.py ，支援多輪 Tool-Use 場景下的 GRPO / CISPO RLAIF / Agentic RL 訓練流程完成 rollout engine 解耦，支援更靈活地切換生成後端 serve_openai_api.py 與 web_demo.py 新增 reasoning_content / tool_calls / open_thinking 支援 Tokenizer 基於 BPE + ByteLevel 更新，並新增工具呼叫與思考標記，預留 buffer token 便於後續擴展 新增 LoRA 權重合並匯出流程，可通過 scripts/convert_model.py 將基礎模型與 LoRA 權重合併為新的完整模型權重 結構圖資源更新，README 大面積更新 2025-10-24 🔥 新增RLAIF訓練演算法：PPO、GRPO、SPO（從0原生實現） 新增斷點續訓功能：支援訓練自動恢復、跨GPU數量恢復、wandb記錄連續性 新增RLAIF資料集：rlaif-mini.jsonl（從SFT資料隨機取樣1萬條）；簡化DPO資料集，加入中文資料 新增YaRN演算法：支援RoPE長文本外推，提升長序列處理能力 Adaptive Thinking：Reason模型可選是否啟用思考鏈 chat_template全面支援Tool Calling和Reasoning標籤（ <tool_call> 、 <think> 等） 新增RLAIF完整章節、訓練曲線對比、演算法原理摺疊說明 SwanLab 替代WandB（國內訪問友好，API完全相容） 規範化所有程式碼 & 修復一些已知bugs 2025-04-26 重要更新 如有相容性需要，可訪問 🔗舊倉庫內容🔗 。 MiniMind模型參數完全改名，對齊Transformers庫模型（統一命名）。 generate方式重構，繼承自GenerationMixin類。 🔥支援llama.cpp、vllm、ollama等熱門三方生態。 規範程式碼和目錄結構。 改動詞表 <s></s> -> <|im_start|><|im_end|> 為相容第三方推理框架llama.cpp、vllm，本次更新需付出一些可觀代價。
本次更新不再支援「直接」載入25-04-26以前的舊模型進行推理。
由於Llama位置編碼方式與minimind存在區別，導致對映Llama模型後QK值存在差異
minimind2系列舊模型均經過權重對映+（微調訓練）QKVO線性層校準恢復而來。
本次更新後將放棄對`minimind-v1`全系列的維護，並在倉庫中下線。 More... 2025-02-09 迎來發布以來重大更新，Release minimind2 Series。 程式碼幾乎全部重構，使用更簡潔明瞭的統一結構。
如有舊程式碼的相容性需要，可訪問 🔗舊倉庫內容🔗 。 免去資料預處理步驟。統一資料集格式，更換為 jsonl 格式杜絕資料集下載混亂的問題。 minimind2系列效果相比MiniMind-V1顯著提升。 小問題：{kv-cache寫法更標準、MoE的負載均衡loss被考慮等等} 提供模型遷移到私有資料集的訓練方案（醫療模型、自我認知樣例）。 精簡預訓練資料集，並大幅提升預訓練資料質量，大幅縮短個人快速訓練所需時間，單卡3090即可2小時復現！ 更新：LoRA微調脫離peft包裝，從0實現LoRA過程；DPO演算法從0使用PyTorch原生實現；模型白盒蒸餾原生實現。 minimind2-DeepSeek-R1系列蒸餾模型誕生！ minimind2具備一定的英文能力！ 更新minimind2與第三方模型的基於更多大模型榜單測試效能的結果。 2024-10-05 為MiniMind拓展了多模態能力之---視覺 移步孿生專案 minimind-v 檢視詳情！ 2024-09-27 09-27更新pretrain資料集的預處理方式，為了保證文本完整性，放棄預處理成.bin訓練的形式（輕微犧牲訓練速度）。 目前pretrain預處理後的檔案命名為：pretrain_data.csv。 刪除了一些冗餘的程式碼。 2024-09-17 更新minimind-v1-moe模型 為了防止歧義，不再使用mistral_tokenizer分詞，全部採用自定義的minimind_tokenizer作為分詞器。 2024-09-01 更新minimind-v1 (108M)模型，採用minimind_tokenizer，預訓練輪次3 + SFT輪次10，更充分訓練，效能更強。 專案已部署至ModelScope創空間，可以在此網站上體驗： 🔗ModelScope線上體驗🔗 2024-08-27 專案首次開源 📌 快速開始 本人的軟硬體配置（供參考） CPU: Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-10980XE CPU @ 3.00GHz RAM: 128 GB GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 (24GB) * 8 Ubuntu==20.04 CUDA==12.2 Python==3.10.16 requirements.txt 第0步 # 克隆倉庫、安裝依賴 git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/jingyaogong/minimind cd minimind && pip install -r requirements.txt -i https://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple Ⅰ 🚀 模型推理 1' 下載模型 在專案根目錄： # 方式1 modelscope download --model gongjy/minimind-3 --local_dir ./minimind-3 # 方式2 git clone https://huggingface.co/jingyaogong/minimind-3 2' CLI 推理 # 方式1：使用 Transformers 格式模型 python eval_llm.py --load_from ./minimind-3 # 方式2：基於 PyTorch 模型（確保./out目錄下有對應權重） python eval_llm.py --load_from ./model --weight full_sft 3'（可選）WebUI # 可能需要`python>=3.10`，安裝 `pip install streamlit` # ⚠️ 須先將 transformers 格式模型資料夾複製到 ./scripts/ 目錄下（例如：cp -r minimind-3 ./scripts/minimind-3），web_demo 指令碼會自動掃描該目錄下包含權重檔案的子資料夾，如不存在則報錯 cd scripts && streamlit run web_demo.py 4'（可選）第三方推理框架 # ollama ollama run jingyaogong/minimind-3 # vllm vllm serve /path/to/model --served-model-name " minimind " Ⅱ 🛠️ 模型訓練 注：提前確認 Torch 的可用後端 import torch print ( torch . cuda . is_available ()) 若你計劃使用 CUDA 訓練，建議先確認當前環境是否已正確識別 GPU。 若 cuda 不可用，也仍可根據自身裝置選擇 CPU 或 MPS 執行，但訓練速度與相容性會有非常大的差異。 如需安裝或更換 PyTorch 版本，可參考 torch_stable 與 連結 1' 下載資料 從下文提供的 資料集下載連結 下載所需資料檔案，並放入 ./dataset 目錄 當前預設僅需下載 pretrain_t2t_mini.jsonl 與 sft_t2t_mini.jsonl ，即可較快復現 MiniMind Zero 對話模型。
如有更多需求，下文提供多種搭配方案，可根據自身任務目標與 GPU 資源靈活選擇。 2' 開始訓練 💡 檢查點暫停續訓 所有訓練指令碼均支援檢查點儲存。新增 --from_resume 1 參數後，即可自動檢測並恢復訓練進度： python train_pretrain.py --from_resume 1
python train_full_sft.py --from_resume 1 # ... 斷點續訓說明： 訓練過程會自動在 ./checkpoints/ 目錄儲存完整檢查點（模型、最佳化器、訓練進度等） 檢查點檔案命名： <權重名>_<維度>_resume.pth （如： full_sft_512_resume.pth ） 支援跨不同 GPU 數量恢復（自動調整 step） 支援 wandb 訓練記錄連續性（自動恢復同一個 run） 適合長時間訓練或不穩定環境，無需擔心訓練中斷導致進度丟失 2.1 預訓練（必須） cd trainer && python train_pretrain.py 訓練後，將得到 out/pretrain_*.pth 作為輸出權重（其中 * 為模型 dimension，預設為 768 ） 2.2 指令微調（必須） cd trainer && python train_full_sft.py 訓練後，將得到 out/full_sft_*.pth 作為輸出權重（其中 full 表示全參數微調） 2.3 測試已訓練模型（可選） 確保待測試的模型 *.pth 檔案位於 ./out/ 目錄下；也可直接前往 此處 下載我已訓練好的 *.pth 權重。 python eval_llm.py --weight full_sft --weight 用於指定權重名稱字首，例如 pretrain 、 full_sft 等；更多參數可直接參考 eval_llm.py 注：其它須知 1、所有訓練指令碼均基於 PyTorch 原生實現，並支援多卡加速。 2、若你的裝置有 N (N > 1) 張顯示卡，可通過以下方式啟動單機 N 卡訓練（DDP，也支援擴展到多機多卡）： torchrun --nproc_per_node N train_xxx.py 3、可根據需要開啟 wandb 記錄訓練過程。 ... train_xxx.py --use_wandb 2025 年 6 月後，國內網路環境通常無法直連 WandB。MiniMind 當前預設轉為使用 SwanLab 作為訓練視覺化工具，其介面與 WandB 基本相容；通常只需將 import wandb 替換為 import swanlab as wandb ，其餘呼叫方式基本無需改動。 📌 資料介紹 Ⅰ Tokenizer 分詞器可以粗略理解成 LLM 使用的一本“詞典”，負責把自然語言對映成 token id，再把 token id 解碼迴文本；專案中也提供了 train_tokenizer.py 作為詞表訓練示例。不建議重新訓練 tokenizer，因為詞表和切分規則一旦變化，模型權重、資料格式、推理介面與社群生態的相容性都會下降，也會削弱模型的傳播性。同時，tokenizer 還會影響 PPL 這類按 token 統計的指標，因此跨 tokenizer 比較時，BPB（Bits Per Byte）往往更有參考價值，可參考 這篇 。

github.title: p-e-w/heretic
github.abstract:
Heretic Training-free language model modification Remove censorship , suppress slop, reduce sycophancy, and more. All in an afternoon, on your gaming PC. Modify any LLM that you can run on your hardware 1 Heretic is a unique tool that lets you do what only corporations with access
to massive computing power usually do: Modify, rather than merely run,
language models. It does not perform expensive training; rather, it uses
a collection of mathematical techniques to steer behavior based on contrasting
example prompts and matching scorers. Heretic can, depending on the configuration: Suppress refusals/remove censorship (this is the default action ) Reduce slop ( config.noslop.toml ) Reduce humor ( config.nohumor.toml ) Reduce sycophancy ( config.nosyco.toml ) Alter emotional alignment ( config.emotions.toml ) Shorten response length ( config.terse.toml ) and many, many other things. ‼️ Using Heretic does NOT require understanding how language models work internally ‼️ In fact, you can go from zero to removing censorship from your first model in a matter of seconds . Heretic supports most dense models, including
many multimodal models, several different MoE architectures, and many modern
hybrid models. The community has created and published thousands of models with Heretic.
Heretic models have been independently benchmarked using standard metrics
like MMLU and GSM8K, and have been found to compare favorably against models
produced with competing abliteration tools. 2 3 Usage Prepare a Python 3.10+ environment with PyTorch 2.6+ installed as appropriate
for your hardware. Then run: pip install -U heretic-llm
heretic Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 Replace Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 with whatever model you want to process. By default, Heretic performs censorship removal (refusal suppression). If you want to do something else, choose one of the configuration files linked
above, or write your own. See config.default.toml for available configuration options. Heretic loads the configuration from config.toml in the working directory by default, or from the file path in the HERETIC_CONFIG_FILE environment variable. Important Configuration files made for Heretic 1.x are not compatible with Heretic 2.x!
See the migration guide for what you need to change
in order to make your old configurations work. At the start of a program run, Heretic benchmarks the system to determine
the optimal batch size to make the most of the available hardware.
On an RTX 3090, with the default configuration, processing Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 takes about 30-40 minutes. After Heretic has finished processing a model, you are given the choice to
save the model, upload it to Hugging Face, chat with it to test how well it works,
run standard benchmarks on it, or any combination of those actions. Controlling what Heretic does using scorer plugins Heretic steers model behavior by optimizing one or multiple scores. Scores are
computed by scorer plugins. You can easily write your own scorers to get full
control over what Heretic does to models. The Scorer interface (abstract base class) your scorer needs to inherit from
is defined in scorer.py . The only required method
is get_score , but there is more machinery (such as settings management)
available when you need it. By default, Heretic scores models by refusal rate (implemented in keyword_rate.py ) and KL divergence
(implemented in kl_divergence.py ).
Additional scorers are available in the scorers directory .
These scorers can serve as examples for your own implementations, and can easily
be adapted to your needs. Scorers are configured through the main configuration file .
Which scorer plugins are active is determined by the scorers setting, which
also controls whether a scorer's score should be minimized or maximized during
optimization. Any number of scorers can be used simultaneously, and their scores
will be co-optimized. Multiple instances of the same scorer can be configured
with different settings. See the configuration file for the full documentation
of this mechanism. The path to a scorer plugin can be specified either as a fully qualified import
path ( fully.qualified.module.MyScorerClass ) or as a file path followed by
a class name ( path/to/plugin.py:MyScorerClass ). You do not have to modify
the Heretic package code in order to use your own plugins. Heretic also has modifier plugins, which are described in the next section . How Heretic works Heretic combines a pluggable modifier (interface in modifier.py ) with a TPE-based hyperparameter optimizer
powered by Optuna . The optimizer finds a set of parameters that,
when passed to the modifier, minimize or maximize a set of configurable scores on the resulting model ( see above ). Heretic ships with two modifiers: Arbitrary-Rank Ablation (ARA) 4 : This is the default modifier, and was
specifically developed for use in Heretic. You can find an overview of how ARA
works in the original pull request ,
and see the precise implementation in ara.py . Directional ablation aka "abliteration" 5 : The classic method for refusal
suppression. Heretic's implementation uses a flexible ablation weight kernel over
the layers, and supports both projected abliteration 6 and norm preservation (MPOA) 7 .
The complete code is in abliteration.py . You can use the modifiers setting to switch between modifier implementations.
Despite the name of the setting using a plural form, Heretic currently allows
only a single modifier for a given processing run. This may change in the future. Reproducibility and the Heretic Grimoire Heretic has the ability to create reproducible models whose repositories contain
all information required to produce a byte-for-byte identical model on demand,
provided that the environment is perfectly identical to the original one. PyTorch
doesn't guarantee that operations return identical outputs unless hardware, drivers,
operating system, and the entire software stack including all package versions
are exactly the same. Heretic manages all that complexity for you. When uploading a processed model to
Hugging Face, Heretic offers to include reproducibility information. This is entirely
optional, but if you choose to do so, the uploaded repository will contain a reproduce folder with detailed instructions for recreating the model
( example ).
This folder contains both human-readable instructions and a machine-readable manifest
file named reproduce.json , which includes all the information Heretic needs to automatically reproduce the model. Automatic reproduction can be performed with heretic --reproduce path/to/reproduce.json Heretic will guide you through the process, checking your environment against the one
that was used to create the model, and pointing out potentially problematic mismatches.
The multi-hour computations that were required to make the original model do not have to be re-done, and the entire process typically takes a few minutes. After you
have exported the resulting model, Heretic will verify the hashes of the weight files
against those stored in the reproduction manifest (they may or may not be identical,
depending on how closely your system resembles the original one). Many people have uploaded models with reproducibility information to Hugging Face.
Since a reproduction manifest is only around 9 kilobytes in size, these manifests
form a portable library of models that can be reproduced at will. That library is called the Heretic Grimoire. You can view it here . But you don't have to rely on an externally hosted web application to access the
library of manifests: The Grimoire is fundamentally designed as a distributed system,
and you can fetch your own local copies of publicly available manifests from
Hugging Face whenever you want by running heretic --collect-reproducibles path/to/target/folder/ You now have a local backup of all reproducible Heretic models, properly catalogued.
To update this collection, simply run the command again.

github.title: colbymchenry/codegraph
github.abstract:
CodeGraph Already installed? Run codegraph upgrade Follow @getcodegraph on X for updates. Supercharge Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, Hermes Agent, Gemini, Antigravity, Kiro, GitHub Copilot, and more with Semantic Code Intelligence The fastest complete code graph · surgical context · built for how agents actually work · 100% local **Kernel powered by Rust** Documentation & Website → The CodeGraph platform is coming — for every PR, know exactly what to test, what could break, which flows are affected, and whether business logic is compromised. Get early beta access to the hosted product · getcodegraph.com Contents Get Started Language Support Why CodeGraph? Key Features Framework-aware Routes Mixed iOS / React Native / Expo bridging Quick Start How It Works CLI Reference MCP Tools Library Usage Configuration Telemetry Verified releases Supported Platforms Supported Agents Supported Languages Measured cross-file coverage Troubleshooting Contributing License Get Started 1. Install the CLI No Node.js required — one command grabs the right build for your OS: # macOS / Linux curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/colbymchenry/codegraph/main/install.sh | sh # Windows (PowerShell) irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/colbymchenry/codegraph/main/install.ps1 | iex Already have Node? Use npm instead (works on any version) npm i -g @colbymchenry/codegraph CodeGraph bundles its own runtime — nothing to compile, no native build, works the same everywhere. The installer puts codegraph on your PATH but doesn't change your current shell — open a new terminal before the next step so the command resolves. Upgrade any time with codegraph upgrade — it detects how you installed (bundle, npm, or npx) and updates in place. Add --check to see if an update is available, or codegraph upgrade <version> to pin one. After an upgrade, codegraph status and your agent tell you when a project's index was built by an older version: run codegraph index there to rebuild it. 2. Wire up your agent(s) In a new terminal , run the installer to connect CodeGraph to the agents you use: codegraph install Detects and auto-configures Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, opencode, Hermes Agent, Gemini CLI, Antigravity IDE, Kiro, GitHub Copilot (VS Code, Copilot CLI, JetBrains IDEs), IBM Bob, Factory Droid, Windsurf, Qwen Code, DeepSeek Harness, Grok Build, Kimi Code, Qoder CLI, and Pi — wiring the CodeGraph MCP server into each. This is the step that connects CodeGraph to your agent; installing the CLI in step 1 does not do it on its own. It only wires up your agent — it does not index any code; building each project's graph is the separate codegraph init in step 3. (Shortcut: npx @colbymchenry/codegraph downloads and runs this in one go.) 3. Initialize each project cd your-project
codegraph init codegraph init creates the local .codegraph/ directory and builds the full graph in the same step — one command, done. 4. No more syncing! Auto-sync is enabled by default. CodeGraph watches the project and updates the graph on every file change — while your agent edits code, or you add, modify, or delete files. The index is never stale, and there is nothing to re-run. Uninstall Changed your mind? One command removes CodeGraph from every agent it configured and the CLI itself — every install it finds (standalone bundle, npm global package, launcher link), shown to you before anything is deleted: codegraph uninstall Pass --keep-cli to remove only the agent configurations and keep the CLI installed. Reverses the installer — strips CodeGraph's MCP server config, instructions, and permissions from each configured agent. Your project indexes ( .codegraph/ ) are left untouched; remove those per-project with codegraph uninit . Use --target to remove from specific agents, or --yes to run non-interactively. Language Support Every language below gets the same treatment — full structural extraction and cross-file resolution into one graph, no per-language setup: Per-language details — extensions, frameworks, and what exactly gets extracted — in Supported Languages . Why CodeGraph? When an AI agent needs to understand code — to answer a question or make a change — it discovers structure the slow way: grep, glob, and Read, one file at a time, rebuilding call paths and dependencies by hand. That's a pile of tool calls and round-trips before it even starts the real work. CodeGraph hands the agent the exact code it needs in one call. It's a pre-built knowledge graph of every symbol, call edge, and dependency in your codebase — so instead of crawling files, the agent asks one question and gets back the relevant source, the call paths between those symbols (including dynamic-dispatch hops grep can't follow), and the blast radius of a change. Surgical context, not a file-by-file search — which means fewer tool calls and faster answers on every codebase, large or small. A note on cost: CodeGraph's win on every codebase is precision — the agent stops crawling files and answers from the graph. On current models that precision is also a large direct saving: the 2026-08 re-measurement, on a harness that blocks the CLI in both arms, put it at 44% lower cost and 62% fewer tokens on average across the seven benchmark repos, because a strong model without the graph burns its budget re-deriving structure. Cost tracks how much discovery a question demands more than raw repo size: 57–78% on questions the file-reading agent needed 28–43 tool calls to answer, near-even where it got there in 7. A note on context: the numbers above measure throughput — tokens processed, tools called, dollars spent to reach one answer. They don't measure what is still sitting in your context window afterward, and on that axis CodeGraph costs more , not less. Across the same seven repos in multi-turn sessions, CodeGraph's responses leave about 80% more retrieval context resident at the end of a session than a file-reading agent's do — on VS Code, 67k tokens against 18k. The mechanism is the same one that makes it fast: CodeGraph returns one dense, verbatim payload that answers the question and then stays in the window, where a grep-and-read agent churns through many small results that get evicted. Fewer tokens processed and a larger persistent footprint are both real at once. If you run long sessions in a small window, budget for it. Measured per-repo: docs/benchmarks/residual-context-occupancy.md . Benchmark Results Tested across 7 real-world open-source codebases spanning 7 languages, comparing an agent (Claude Code, headless) answering one architecture question with and without CodeGraph, at the median of 4 runs per arm . Re-measured 2026-08-05 on Claude Opus 4.8 against the current build, on a harness that blocks the codegraph CLI in both arms — contamination row: 0 of 28 without-arm runs. The universal win — every repo, every size: 88% fewer tool calls · 53% faster · 62% fewer tokens · 44% cheaper · file reads cut to zero on all seven repos. With the index available, the agent answers from one to four codegraph_explore calls and stops. Without it, the agent burns its budget on discovery — up to 43 tool calls and 19 file reads re-deriving what the graph already knew. Every repo was faster with CodeGraph in this measurement — by 35% on the narrowest question, by 3.6× on the widest. Codebase Language Tool calls Time File reads Tokens Cost VS Code TypeScript · ~11k files 2 vs 28 2.2× faster (58s vs 2m 10s) 0 vs 12 77% fewer 71% cheaper Excalidraw TypeScript · ~640 2 vs 43 3.6× faster (45s vs 2m 42s) 0 vs 18 84% fewer 78% cheaper Django Python · ~3k 3 vs 14 35% faster (54s vs 1m 23s) 0 vs 8.5 41% fewer 13% cheaper¹ Tokio Rust · ~790 3 vs 29 2.6× faster (1m 3s vs 2m 43s) 0 vs 19 65% fewer 64% cheaper OkHttp Java · ~645 1 vs 6 43% faster (33s vs 58s) 0 vs 2 54% fewer 21% cheaper Gin Go · ~110 1 vs 7 39% faster (28s vs 46s) 0 vs 4 52% fewer ~even¹ Alamofire Swift · ~110 4 vs 33 2.6× faster (54s vs 2m 22s) 0 vs 16.

github.abstract:
Arnis Arnis creates complex and accurate Minecraft Java Edition (1.21.4+), Bedrock Edition, Luanti (Minetest) and Hytale worlds that reflect real-world geography, topography, and architecture. This free and open source project is designed to handle large-scale geographic data from the real world and generate detailed Minecraft worlds. The algorithm processes geospatial data from OpenStreetMap as well as elevation data to create an accurate Minecraft representation of terrain and architecture.
Generate your hometown, big cities, and natural landscapes with ease! Want mobile generation or larger map sizes? MapSmith generates worlds in your browser, no install required. This GitHub page and arnismc.com are the only official project websites. Do not download Arnis from any other website. ⌨️ Usage Download the latest release or compile the project on your own. Choose your area on the map using the rectangle tool, then simply click on Start Generation !
Additionally, you can customize various generation settings, such as world scale, spawn point, or building interior generation. 📚 Documentation Full documentation is available in the GitHub Wiki , covering topics such as generation settings, command line usage, technical explanations, FAQs and contribution guidelines. backgroundvid.webm 🏆 Open Source Key objectives of this project Modularity : Ensure that all components (e.g., data fetching, processing, and world generation) are cleanly separated into distinct modules for better maintainability and scalability. Performance Optimization : We aim to maintain strong performance and fast world generation. Comprehensive Documentation : Detailed in-code documentation for a clear structure and logic. User-Friendly Experience : Focus on making the project easy to use for end users. Cross-Platform Support : We want this project to run smoothly on Windows, macOS, and Linux. How to contribute This project is open source and welcomes contributions from everyone! Whether you're interested in fixing bugs, improving performance, adding new features, or enhancing documentation, your input is valuable. Simply fork the repository, make your changes, and submit a pull request. Please respect the above-mentioned key objectives. Contributions of all levels are appreciated, and your efforts help improve this tool for everyone. Command line Build: cargo run --release --no-default-features -- --output-dir="C:/YOUR_PATH/.minecraft/saves" --bbox="min_lat,min_lng,max_lat,max_lng" GUI Build: cargo run --release All command line options, like the generation modes, winter and One World, are explained on the Command Line Usage wiki page. After your pull request is merged, I will take care of regularly creating update releases which will include your changes. If you are using Nix, you can run the program directly with nix run github:louis-e/arnis -- --output-dir=YOUR_PATH/.minecraft/saves --bbox="min_lat,min_lng,max_lat,max_lng" ⭐ Star History 📰 Academic & Press Recognition Arnis has been recognized in various academic and press publications after gaining more attention in December 2024. Building realistic Minecraft worlds with Open Data on AWS: How Arnis uses elevation datasets at scale Floodcraft: Game-based Interactive Learning Environment using Minecraft for Flood Mitigation and Preparedness for K-12 Education Hackaday: Bringing OpenStreetMap Data into Minecraft TomsHardware: Minecraft Tool Lets You Create Scale Replicas of Real-World Locations XDA Developers: Hometown Minecraft Map: Arnis Free to use press assets, including screenshots and logos, can be found here . 🔒 Code Signing Policy Free code signing provided by SignPath.io , certificate by SignPath Foundation . The Windows executable is built from this repository by the release workflow on GitHub-hosted runners and is only signed after a maintainer approves the signing request. All roles (committer, reviewer and approver) are held by louis-⁠e . [2024/12] We are working with the vLLM community to support [RFC]: Hardware pluggable . Overview vLLM Ascend ( vllm-ascend ) is a community maintained hardware plugin for running vLLM seamlessly on the Huawei Ascend NPU. It is the recommended approach for supporting the Ascend backend within the vLLM community. It adheres to the principles outlined in the [RFC]: Hardware pluggable , providing a hardware-pluggable interface that decouples the integration of the Ascend NPU with vLLM. By using vLLM Ascend plugin, popular open-source models, including Transformer-like, Mixture-of-Experts (MoE), Embedding, Multi-modal LLMs can run seamlessly on the Ascend NPU. For detailed information on supported models and features, please refer to the Support Matrix . DeepWiki DeepWiki is a dynamic knowledge base collaboratively maintained by the community and AI, designed to provide you with deeper technical insights beyond conventional documentation. If official documentation serves as a "quick start" guide to help you get going, the DeepWiki is your technical companion for "deep understanding". Here, you can explore: core architecture and design principles, key source code interpretations, technical context, and decision-making logic. Whether you are a performance tuner looking to deploy vllm-ascend in production or a contributor aiming to build upon it for secondary development, DeepWiki offers invaluable references for you. Welcome to explore now and join us in delving deep into the technical core of vLLM-Ascend. Prerequisites Hardware: Atlas 800I A2 series, Atlas 800I A3 series, Atlas 300I Duo, 950PR&950DT Products OS: Linux Software: Python == 3.12 CANN == 9.2.1 (For Ascend HDK version, please refer to the Release Notes ) PyTorch == 2.10.0, TorchNPU == 2.10.0.post7 vLLM (the same version as vllm-ascend) Accessing Ascend NPU If you need to access Ascend NPU computing resources for development or testing, please visit the HiDevLab - Online Development page on the HiDevLab platform to apply for and use them. Getting Started Please use the following recommended versions to get started quickly: Version Release type Doc v0.30.0 Latest stable version See QuickStart and Installation for more details v0.23.0 Stable version See QuickStart and Installation for more details Branch vllm-ascend has a main branch and a dev branch. main : main branch, corresponds to the vLLM main branch, and is continuously monitored for quality through Ascend CI. releases/vX.Y.Z : development branch, created alongside new releases of vLLM. others.title: Artificial Intelligence in Science and Physics Education, 2015-2026: An AI-Assisted Bibliometric and Title-and-Abstract Analysis across Fourteen Journals
others.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) research in science and physics education has expanded rapidly, particularly since the emergence of generative AI. This study maps publication patterns, research characteristics, and citation connections across 14 selected science and physics education journals. OpenAlex searches using fifteen AI-related terms identified 966 unique records published between January 2015 and September 2026. AI-assisted screening retained 333 publications, which were coded using available titles and abstracts. Bibliometric analyses examined publication growth, thematic patterns, and citations within and between the two journal groups. Of the included publications, 87.1% appeared from 2023 onwards. Generative large language models and chatbots accounted for 58.9% of the corpus, while instruction and assessment together represented 48.3% of publications. Among 182 records classified as involving human participants, comparison groups were identifiable in 14.3%, effect sizes in 8.2%, and instrument validity evidence in 5.5%. These frequencies reflect information identifiable in bibliographic records, rather than the absence of these features in the full studies. Laboratory and experimental support was the principal educational function in 27 publications. Citation connections between the journal groups were limited: their reference sets had a Jaccard index of 0.047, and 15.6% of publications cited an included study from the other group. The findings document rapid growth and uneven research emphases within the selected venues. Independent human validation and full-text assessment are needed before drawing firm conclusions about methodological quality or educational effectiveness.

others.title: OmniAct: One Policy, One Million Embodiments
others.abstract: A single policy that controls diverse robots must not only transfer task knowledge across embodiments, but also adapt its behavior to each robot's capabilities. Existing approaches facilitate transfer through shared action representations, but these representations do not necessarily capture how differences in robot morphology should shape manipulation strategies. We introduce OmniAct, a cross-embodiment manipulation policy that conditions directly on each robot's kinematics in a specific scene to produce embodiment-specific behavior. This kinematic graph represents the robot's joint positions, motion axes, and connectivity to its visual observation, allowing the policy to account for how its embodiment related to objects and surfaces in the scene. A flow-matching policy predicts relative joint motions for each node, enabling control across robots with different degrees of freedom and kinematic configurations. To learn how physical structure shapes behavior at scale, we procedurally design and filter one million physically feasible robot embodiments; next, we develop algorithms to generate robot trajectories in simulation for all embodiments; finally, we train across diverse simulated manipulation tasks. On 2,000 embodiment-scene-held-out evaluation episodes, OmniAct achieves 63.0% success, compared to 17.8% for pi 0.5 and 57.9% for the strongest baseline; on the task families GPT-6 Astra was evaluated on, it achieves 64.7% against GPT-6 Astra's 41.1%. On a previously unseen real-world robot, it achieves nearly twice the success rate of the next best method, MolmoAct2. Beyond task success, we observe that OmniAct learns distinct manipulation strategies that exploit the capabilities and accommodate the limitations of different morphologies. Project: https://omniact.github.io/

others.title: PointX: Multi-View Consistent Intrinsics by Querying Surface Points
others.abstract: The appearance of a scene is determined by the albedo, roughness, metallicity and normal of every point on its surface, and by the light that reaches it, its irradiance. Recovering these intrinsics from images is ambiguous, and methods that predict them per pixel give the same surface point a different decomposition in every view. We introduce PointX, a simple feed-forward model that predicts intrinsics per 3D surface point instead. A multi-view transformer encodes a set of unposed images, and for any queried surface point, PointX pools the point's tokens across the views in which it appears and decodes the point's intrinsics once. Each point of a 3D reconstruction of the scene, such as a point cloud or a mesh, thus receives a single prediction, which is exactly consistent across views by construction and enables view-consistent relighting and editing. The same model also predicts per-view maps, from one image or many, by querying the point seen at every pixel. These maps agree across views up to the precision of the estimated geometry and correspondences. PointX is significantly more consistent than existing methods, while remaining competitive in accuracy from a single image and improving as views are added. Project page: https://pointx-paper.github.io/

others.title: DiaCap: Jointly Learning Who Speaks When for Audiovisual Dialogue Captioning
others.abstract: We present DiaCap, an audiovisual LLM for comprehensive dialogue captioning, which produces the transcript, timestamps, and a visual description of the speaker for every utterance in a video. Considering that utterance timing and audiovisual diarization are tightly coupled, DiaCap unifies the tasks in a single model, trained in two complementary stages. First, we train DiaCap on 225K curated clips, using synthetic captions that densely label every utterance in detail. Second, we further refine the model via reinforcement learning on 2.9K human-corrected clips, using fine-grained feedback that directly evaluates utterance timing, speaker grouping, and speaker binding. On DiaDemBench, which we extend with utterance-level timestamps and subtitle redaction, both DiaCap with off-the-shelf transcripts and its end-to-end variant DiaCap-E2E achieve strong results. Specifically, DiaCap performs on par with Gemini 4 Argon in audiovisual diarization while clearly outperforming it in timestamp accuracy (76.59 vs. 42.76 TIME). It also maintains strong diarization on multilingual and minute-long videos, and transfers to audiovisual question answering.

others.title: BioLoom: Scaling Biomedical Vision-Language Models by Learning from the Structure of Scientific Articles
others.abstract: The development of biomedical vision-language models (VLMs) with contrastive image-text pretraining has been driven by scaling to increasingly large and diverse image-text datasets. Beyond scaling, further progress can come from learning richer representations from existing data. We hypothesize that the structure of scientific literature itself provides an additional source of supervision: figures, panels, captions, and accompanying article text encode rich relationships across modalities. Yet, treating these as independent image-text pairs overlooks their relationships. To address this limitation, we incorporate these structural relationships into contrastive image-text supervision. We preserve exact image-text matches while introducing weaker positive supervision for related pairs, such as a panel and the caption of a sibling panel. We upweight cross-article negatives of the same content type to encourage finer discrimination. We also enrich panel descriptions using visual content, original figure captions, and mentioning paragraphs. Pairing panels with these descriptions and whole figures with their original captions yields Loom52M, a dataset of 52.4 million image-text pairs spanning scientific charts and biomedical images. Using Loom52M, BioLoom (DFN-2B) achieves 56.82% domain-balanced mean accuracy across 67 zero-shot classification tasks from 43 datasets in 10 domains, compared with 48.77% for MedPMC-CLIP. On BioLoomBench with concise captions and BioMedFlickr, it achieves bidirectional mean Recall@1 of 63.20% and 10.59%, versus 46.37% and 7.55% for the respective strongest evaluated baselines, BiomedCLIP and MedPMC-CLIP. Code, datasets, benchmarks, and models are available at https://bioloom-clip.github.io/.

others.title: CoT-Proxy: Cross-Format Transfer for Distilling Long-Horizon Policies
others.abstract: Reasoning models become long-horizon agents through reinforcement learning or, more cheaply, through fine-tuning on a stronger teacher's trajectories, which contain the teacher's chain-of-thought as well as its actions. The standard fine-tuning approach imitates both, yet the strongest teachers are closed models whose chain-of-thought is hidden behind an API. We show that the chain-of-thought can be left out altogether and that the long-horizon policy can be distilled from the teacher's actions alone. The student is trained on these trajectories with its reasoning block left empty, while a KL loss on a replay buffer of its own generations limits drift from its initial model. Surprisingly, the policy learned from these trajectories with an empty reasoning block carries over to inference with thinking enabled, where the student reasons in its own style while acting like the teacher, an effect we call cross-format transfer. Distilling the actions of Qwen3.6-27B raises the task success of Qwen3-4B on AppWorld from 7% to 18% and that of Qwen3-32B from 12% to 25%. We further introduce CoT-proxies, short summaries of the teacher's reasoning placed after the empty reasoning block, which raise Qwen3-4B further, to 35%. Since neither actions nor CoT-proxies need the hidden chain-of-thought, the recipe applies unchanged to closed teachers. Distilling GPT-5.6 Luna from its visible outputs and the reasoning summaries its API returns raises Qwen3-4B from 7% to 48% on AppWorld and from 3% to 28% on SWE-bench Verified.

others.title: One Take, Many Cameras: Audio-Grounded Shot Synthesis for Dialogue Re-Cinematography
others.abstract: Creating a dialogue scene typically requires cutting between multiple views (e.g., close-ups, medium shots, and over-the-shoulder shots) of the actors. Yet capturing such coverage is costly and in many settings unavailable. We study dialogue re-cinematography: synthesizing additional shots from a single wide-angle dialogue video. Existing video generators can synthesize new shots, but rely on visual cues alone, so when the source video barely shows the lips, the generated lip motion fails to match the speech. Our key observation is that the speech audio is view-invariant: it constrains lip motion in any target view. Building on this insight, we adapt a pretrained audio-visual diffusion model to generate the new shot from a target frame that specifies the view, a source video that contains the performance, and the speech audio that drives lip motion. In multi-person scenes, however, pretrained audio-visual models drive every visible face with the same speech, causing speech leakage, where silent listeners mouth the speaker's words. We therefore introduce speaker-aware audio gating, a training-free module that lets the audio drive only the faces that speak in the target shot. On a cinematic paired-view benchmark spanning diverse viewpoints and framings, our method lowers perceptual error by 59%, landmark error by 56%, and speech leakage by 97% relative to the strongest baseline, Wan 3.0. Our method also remains robust on in-the-wild scenes, highlighting its potential for film post-production.
